metrics.claim_path: no-llm/no-network (structural; the fast claim check is a local HMAC verify)

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a deterministic test that simulates an interrupted run (no `run_finished` marker written) and asserts the status resolves to `stale-running` and recovery launches at most one re-run.
evidence: Plan describes the recovery mechanism: 'A flip that kills an in-flight run costs at most one re-run; a run_finished marker in a finally + a stale-running status read bound the worst case.'

The Tests paragraph enumerates concurrency, basis-ref, post-completion re-call, async-handle latency, poll transition, and fresh-registry durable-verdict tests \u2014 but no test asserting that an interrupted (no run_finished marker) run is observed as stale-running and that recovery re-runs at most once.
E5 checklist: 'Changed/deleted behaviors get corresponding ... test work' and failure-path coverage for a new failure mode the plan itself introduces.
findings.finding: The plan introduces a blue-green-flip / crash recovery path (a `run_finished` marker written in a `finally`, plus a `stale-running` status read that bounds worst-case to one re-run) but the enumerated deterministic test list does not include a test for this recovery path.
findings.location: Approved remediation — "a run_finished marker in a finally + a stale-running status read bound the worst case"; Tests paragraph
scenarios: A blue-green flip mid-run leaves a running-but-orphaned job; without a test, the stale-running detection and at-most-one-rerun bound could regress silently and re-trigger the very duplicate-paid-run cost the plan aims to stop.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Route the docs/mcp-reference.md change through `scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py` (regenerate, don't hand-edit) and ensure the new *_start/*_status/gate_status tools' first docstring paragraphs carry the start+poll guidance the drift gate will publish.
evidence: docs/mcp-reference.md:3 '**Generated by `scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py` — do not edit by hand.** ... a CI drift gate fails the build if this file is stale.'

scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py:5-7 'The reference is DERIVED from the server's OWN registrars ... so a CI drift gate can regenerate it and fail the build on any diff — a newly-registered tool cannot ship undocumented.'
tests/unit/test_gen_mcp_reference.py exists as the drift gate
findings.finding: docs/mcp-reference.md is listed as a hand-edited file-impact target, but it is an auto-generated artifact ('Generated by scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py — do not edit by hand') protected by a CI drift gate; the new *_start/status tool rows are derived from the tool registrars' first docstring paragraph, so a hand edit will either be overwritten or fail the drift gate.
scenarios: Author hand-edits docs/mcp-reference.md; CI drift gate (test_gen_mcp_reference.py / --check) fails because the committed file no longer matches the generator output for the newly-registered *_start/status tools.
findings.suggested_fix: In the file-impact list, replace hand-editing docs/mcp-reference.md with: add the *_start/status tool docstrings, then run `python scripts/gen_mcp_reference.py` and commit the regenerated docs/mcp-reference.md; verify `--check` (test_gen_mcp_reference.py) passes.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Make the post-flip poll path durable: either key the authoritative poll on ticket_id+gate+basis (git-backed attestation state) rather than a git-ignored job_id index, or make the job_id→(ticket,gate,basis) mapping reconstructible from the durable store; state explicitly which poll key survives a blue-green flip for an MCP-only client.
evidence: Plan: 'Durability across a blue-green flip comes from the git-backed verdict ..., not from in-process state' — but the job_id index is a git-ignored local file, not git-backed
Code: .rebar/workflow_runs index is written to the local repo_root (runs.py:55 record_run_location) and is not part of the git-backed store

Code: stateless_http=True is used precisely because a flipped-to container 'never heard of' prior per-container state (mcp_server.py:585-600); the same reasoning applies to a job_id index absent on the new container
Plan proposes polling via plan_review_status (keys on ticket_id) OR a job_id-based gate_status/verify_completion_status — leaving the post-flip poll key ambiguous
findings.finding: Phase 2's job_id→(ticket,gate,basis) resolution depends on a git-ignored, local-only .rebar/gate_runs/<job_id> index that does NOT survive a blue-green container flip, so a poll keyed on job_id after a flip cannot resolve the durable verdict — in tension with the plan's own durability argument and AC #4 (portable / MCP-only client observes completion).
findings.location: Approved remediation — Phase 2 (".rebar/gate_runs/<job_id> index ... maps job_id→(ticket,gate,basis)") and AC #4
scenarios: Agent gets a {job_id,status:'running'} handle from review_plan_start; a blue-green flip swaps containers; agent polls gate_status(job_id) on the new container, which has no .rebar/gate_runs/<job_id> entry and cannot map job_id→ticket
MCP-only hosted client with no checkout relies solely on the returned job_id and cannot fall back to ticket_id
findings.suggested_fix: Define the job_id as a deterministic function of (gate_type, ticket_id, basis SHA, variant) — the same tuple as the dedup key — so gate_status(job_id) can reconstruct (ticket,gate,basis) with no local index, then read the git-backed attestation/sidecar; keep .rebar/gate_runs/ only as a non-authoritative in-process convenience cache.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the exact value vocabulary of the `variant` component of the dedup key, enumerating which per-tool parameters it folds in (e.g. verify_completion's `graph` tri-state, review_plan's non-force axes) so same-key attach and different-key split are both correct.
evidence: Plan: `Dedup key = sha256("\0".join([gate_type, canonicalised ticket_id, resolved 40-hex basis SHA, variant, readonly]))`
`gate_type`, basis SHA, and `readonly` are pinned; `variant` alone is left as a bare token with no enumerated values

src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py verify_completion has a `graph` tri-state (None uses ticket-type default; True/False force subtree/own-criteria) — a distinct semantic axis the key must or must not fold into `variant`
AC#2 requires 'a re-invocation while a review for the same ticket+basis is in flight attaches to that run' — correctness of that attach hinges on the key's exact components
findings.finding: The dedup key formula names a `variant` component whose value vocabulary is never defined, yet it is load-bearing for the AC#2 idempotency guarantee. `verify_completion` takes a `graph` tri-state (None/True/False, per its docstring) and `review_plan` takes `force`; without defining what `variant` encodes, two callers that differ only in `graph` could wrongly share a single verdict, or identical callers could wrongly split into two billable runs.
findings.location: Root cause / Approved remediation — Phase 1, dedup-key definition
scenarios: Two agents call verify_completion for the same ticket+basis but one passes graph=True and the other graph=False; if variant ignores graph they share the wrong verdict
Two identical review_plan calls where one sets force=True: force=True bypasses dedup per the plan, but a non-force retry's variant must be defined to attach correctly
findings.suggested_fix: Specify variant per tool: for verify_completion, variant := the resolved graph mode (subtree|own); for review_plan, variant := a constant (or the source mode) — and state explicitly that force is NOT part of the key (it bypasses dedup) so identical force/non-force calls do not accidentally key-collide.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Define the complete terminal-status enum for the new poll (gate_status / verify_completion_status) and give the explicit mapping from review_plan's PASS|BLOCK|INDETERMINATE and verify_completion's PASS|FAIL into it (or state that the poll returns the raw verdict alongside a running/done phase).
evidence: Plan: 'async-start returns a handle <100ms and poll transitions running->passed/failed'
src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py review_plan docstring: verdict is one of "PASS"|"BLOCK"|"INDETERMINATE"
src/rebar/_mcp_llm.py verify_completion docstring: verdict is "PASS"|"FAIL"

Existing plan_review_status already exposes a rich stale-* / certified / unsigned verdict enum (src/rebar/_mcp_reads.py:179-186), so the new poll's two-valued phrasing is inconsistent with the surface it says it reuses
findings.finding: The poll surface's terminal-status vocabulary is specified only as `running -> passed/failed` (two-valued), but the underlying gate verdicts are not two-valued: review_plan returns PASS|BLOCK|INDETERMINATE and verify_completion returns PASS|FAIL. The plan never defines how a BLOCK or INDETERMINATE plan-review verdict maps into the new gate_status/verify_completion_status enum, so an MCP-only executor polling the handle cannot distinguish a blocking verdict from a hard failure from an indeterminate/not-claimable outcome.
findings.location: Approved remediation — Phase 2 (poll via plan_review_status / verify_completion_status / gate_status) and Fix-plan tests ('poll transitions running->passed/failed')
scenarios: A plan review completes BLOCK; a poller sees 'failed' (or worse, an undefined state) and cannot tell a coachable BLOCK from a transport/execution failure
review_plan fast-fails INDETERMINATE (ticket-not-claimable, no LLM); the poll status for that terminal state is unspecified
findings.suggested_fix: Specify the poll payload as {status: running|done|failed, verdict?: <raw gate verdict>} where verdict carries PASS|BLOCK|INDETERMINATE (plan) / PASS|FAIL (completion) verbatim once status=done, rather than collapsing to passed/failed.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add `src/rebar/_mcp_health.py` to the file-impact inventory: update `CERTIFIED_TOOLS` to include the new `*_start` tools and reconcile `instrument_certified_tools`'s fail-loud async guard with Phase 1 making `review_plan`/`verify_completion` async — derive both via `find_referencing_symbols` on `CERTIFIED_TOOLS` and `instrument_certified_tools` plus a string grep for the tool names in monkeypatch/getattr/test sites.
evidence: Plan: 'The sync review_plan/verify_completion bodies in _mcp_llm.py are wrapped by it (async def + anyio.to_thread).'
Plan file-impact list names _mcp_llm.py/_mcp_writes.py/_mcp_reads.py/_mcp_models.py/gate_runs.py/docs but NOT _mcp_health.py.
_mcp_health.py:47 `CERTIFIED_TOOLS = frozenset({"review_plan", "verify_completion", "review_code", "scan_spec"})` — gates gauge via track() (line 138) and SIGTERM drain (line 174).

_mcp_health.py:160-180 instrument_certified_tools(): 'An already-async CERTIFIED tool here is FAIL-LOUD... would make the SYNC gauge wrapper a no-op... Raising surfaces that in a test' — raises RuntimeError when is_async.
findings.finding: The Phase-1 conversion of `review_plan`/`verify_completion` to `async def` and Phase-2 addition of `*_start` background-LLM tools omit `src/rebar/_mcp_health.py` from the affected-file inventory, though both changed symbols are structurally referenced there: `instrument_certified_tools()` is fail-loud on an async CERTIFIED tool, and `CERTIFIED_TOOLS` gates the in-flight gauge / shutdown-grace drain the plan's own blue-green bound relies on.
findings.location: Fix plan — file impact (Phase 1: `_mcp_llm.py` wrap sync bodies; Phase 2: `*_start`) and 'Approved remediation' ('async def + anyio.to_thread')
scenarios: `instrument_certified_tools` raises RuntimeError at server startup once review_plan/verify_completion become async def, breaking wire_health (unpatched call site → server won't boot).

New `review_plan_start`/`verify_completion_start` background LLM runs are absent from CERTIFIED_TOOLS, so InFlightGauge.track() no-ops them and the SIGTERM/shutdown-grace drain fails open — a blue-green flip can SIGKILL an in-flight paid run, contradicting the plan's 'at most one re-run' bound.
test_mcp_http_transport.py / _mcp_health tests asserting the async-certified fail-loud path become affected and unpatched.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Wire the dedup kill-switch through the existing [tool.rebar.mcp] config schema (auto-derived REBAR_MCP_<KEY_UPPER>) and add it to mcp_server.py's env declaration list, rather than a bespoke os.getenv('REBAR_MCP_DEDUP') read, so it matches the established MCP-toggle seam.
evidence: Plan: "Default-ON with kill-switch env `REBAR_MCP_DEDUP=0`."
_config_schema.py:305/343/369: "REBAR_MCP_<KEY_UPPER> env var" — MCP toggles are auto-derived from [tool.rebar.mcp] config keys
mcp_server.py:127–388 enumerate every MCP env var (READONLY, ALLOW_LLM, ALLOW_JIRA_SYNC, …) as declared config-backed toggles
This is a consistency/config-surface note, not a rebuild-of-existing (no prior dedup registry exists for MCP LLM ops)
findings.finding: The Phase 1 kill-switch is specified as a raw env var REBAR_MCP_DEDUP=0, but the codebase routes MCP toggles through a config schema that auto-derives REBAR_MCP_<KEY_UPPER> from [tool.rebar.mcp] keys (_config_schema.py) and enumerates them in mcp_server.py's env-declaration list; a bespoke os.getenv toggle diverges from that established seam.
scenarios: Operator expects the dedup toggle to be settable via [tool.rebar.mcp] like every other MCP switch, or discoverable in the server's env declaration list, but it is a raw env-only flag.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a boolean key (e.g. `dedup`, default true) to the [tool.rebar.mcp] config section so REBAR_MCP_DEDUP is auto-derived and declared alongside READONLY/ALLOW_LLM in mcp_server.py.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Decide and state whether the poll surface is a per-gate verify_completion_status or a single generic gate_status, so the documented contract (AC#3) is unambiguous.
evidence: 'Poll via the existing plan_review_status plus a new verify_completion_status (or a single generic gate_status).'
AC #3 requires 'the chosen contract (start+poll)' be documented — but the plan does not decide which of the two poll shapes is 'the chosen contract'.
findings.finding: The poll surface for verify_completion is left as an unresolved either/or ('a new verify_completion_status (or a single generic gate_status')), deferring the contract choice to the executor.
scenarios: Two implementers could ship different poll tool names/shapes; docs (AC#3) can't be written until the choice is made.

evidence: 1 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Add AGENTS.md to the 'Fix plan — file impact' edit set (Phase 2) so the *_start+poll steering the remediation prose promises actually lands in the MCP-mandate document.
evidence: Remediation Phase 2: 'AGENTS.md + docstrings + docs/mcp-reference.md + docs/plan-review-gate.md steer agents to `*_start`+poll for long ops.'
Fix plan — file impact lists only docs/mcp-reference.md and docs/plan-review-gate.md (plus code/test files) — AGENTS.md is absent.
AGENTS.md:118-132 is the section that mandates driving the tracker through MCP and points to docs/mcp-reference.md; the Summary calls this 'the path AGENTS.md *mandates*.'
findings.finding: AGENTS.md is named in the remediation prose as a file that will steer agents to *_start+poll and is the document that mandates routing gate ops through MCP, but it is omitted from the 'Fix plan — file impact' edit-set enumeration.
findings.location: Fix plan — file impact vs. Approved remediation Phase 2 ('AGENTS.md + docstrings + docs/mcp-reference.md + docs/plan-review-gate.md steer agents')
scenarios: Implementer works from the file-impact list, edits only the docs/ files, and leaves AGENTS.md (the mandate document) without the *_start/poll guidance the remediation says it should carry.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify the retire/cleanup lifecycle for `.rebar/gate_runs/<job_id>` index entries (TTL/sweep or purge-on-terminal-status), mirroring the purge policy chosen for `.rebar/workflow_runs/`.
evidence: Plan defines create ('A git-ignored .rebar/gate_runs/<job_id> index ... maps job_id->(ticket,gate,basis)') and a run_finished marker, but never states when/if these per-job index files are removed or pruned.
T9 checklist: 'There is a RETIRE/cleanup path — it doesn\u2019t leak/accumulate.'
findings.finding: The git-ignored `.rebar/gate_runs/<job_id>` index has a defined create path (on `*_start`) but no stated RETIRE/cleanup path, so job_id index entries accumulate without bound as gate runs complete.
scenarios: A long-lived MCP server accrues one .rebar/gate_runs/<job_id> file per gate run indefinitely; over many tickets the index directory grows unbounded.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the defensive max-age sweep threshold (a concrete default) and whether it is env-configurable, noting it is defensive-only since correctness relies on purge-on-completion.
evidence: 'Purge-on-completion (correctness needs no TTL) + a defensive max-age sweep.'
No max-age value or config knob is named for the sweep, though it is a tunable.
findings.finding: The 'defensive max-age sweep' threshold for the in-flight registry is asserted without a stated value or whether it is configurable.
findings.location: Approved remediation — Phase 1; Fix plan file impact (_mcp_inflight.py)
scenarios: An implementer must pick an arbitrary max-age for the defensive sweep without guidance.
findings.suggested_fix: Name a default (e.g. sweep entries older than a stated multiple of the gate-duration guidance, ~30 min) behind an env override, and note correctness does not depend on it.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the atomic primitive (a lock/CAS around the registry map mutation) that makes the check-then-register step in `_mcp_inflight.py` race-free under concurrent same-key callers.
evidence: Plan: 'an in-process singleflight registry (golang singleflight semantics: a second concurrent caller for the same key awaits the SAME computation and shares its verdict)'.
T9 checklist: 'Shared/mutable state mutated atomically (lock/CAS/transaction, no check-then-act TOCTOU).' The plan states the desired semantics but not the guarding primitive.
findings.finding: The plan asserts golang `singleflight` semantics for the in-flight registry but does not name the concrete atomic mechanism (lock/CAS) guarding the check-then-register step, leaving the TOCTOU-critical 'is there an in-flight entry? -> register mine' operation unspecified for the reviewer to confirm race-freedom.
scenarios: Two concurrent same-key callers arriving within the check-then-register window each register a computation if the registry mutation is not atomic, launching two billable LLM runs — the exact defect AC #2 must prevent.
